turn1.explanation: The unit fires most strongly on tokens that spell a bird name, whether the word means the bird or not: surnames (Finch, Swan, Heron, Falcon), idioms (lame duck, green swan), titles (Swan Lake), band names (Flamingos), function names (Kestrel) and acronyms (SWAN). Separately and more weakly (about 5-7), it fires on abbreviated month names written before a day number, such as "Oct. 13", "Aug. 10" and "23 Sep 16".
turn1.evidence: All 12 top examples peak on bird-word tokens, often in non-bird senses: "Run-Kestrel", "Yvik Swan", the SWAN MRI sequence, "Robert Falcon Scott" and "The Flamingos". All 8 mid-range examples peak on month abbreviations in dates (Sep, Oct, Nov, Aug, Feb, Sept), which share nothing obvious with birds.
turn1.missing_data: Three kinds of input would change this answer: plain bird words in literal ornithological text, to check whether literal uses fire as strongly as name uses; non-bird animal names; and month names that are spelled out or not abbreviated, to see whether the date trigger is really about abbreviations.
